_meta.indication: VABYSMO is a VEGF and Ang-2 inhibitor indicated for the treatment of patients with Neovascular (wet) Age-Related Macular Degeneration (nAMD) and Diabetic Macular Edema (DME).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-masked, active comparator (aflibercept)-controlled, 2-year studies; patients randomized 1:1 to aflibercept 2 mg Q8W after three initial monthly doses or VABYSMO 6 mg every 4 weeks for the first 4 doses followed by dosing up to every 16 weeks (Q16W).
pivotal_trials.population: Newly diagnosed, treatment-naive patients with neovascular (wet) AMD; ages 50 to 99, mean 75.9 years.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change from baseline in BCVA (ETDRS letter score) averaged over the week 40, 44, and 48 visits; non-inferiority margin of −4 letters.
pivotal_trials.n: 1,329 enrolled; TENAYA VABYSMO N=334, aflibercept N=337; LUCERNE VABYSMO N=331, aflibercept N=327
pivotal_trials.result: VABYSMO non-inferior to aflibercept. TENAYA mean BCVA change 5.8 (95% CI 4.6, 7.1) vs 5.1 (3.9, 6.4), difference in LS mean 0.7 (-1.1, 2.5); LUCERNE 6.6 (5.3, 7.8) vs 6.6 (5.3, 7.8), difference in LS mean 0.0 (-1.7, 1.8).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-masked, active comparator-controlled 2-year studies; patients randomized 1:1:1 to aflibercept Q8W (after 5 monthly doses), VABYSMO Q8W (after 6 monthly doses), or VABYSMO Variable dosing.
pivotal_trials.population: Diabetic patients with DME; ages 24 to 91, mean 62.2 years; 78% anti-VEGF naive and 22% previously treated with a VEGF inhibitor.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change from baseline in BCVA (ETDRS letter score) at year 1 (average of week 48, 52, and 56 visits); non-inferiority margin of −4 letters.
pivotal_trials.n: 1,891 enrolled; YOSEMITE VABYSMO Q8W N=315, Variable N=313, aflibercept N=312; RHINE VABYSMO Q8W N=317, Variable N=319, aflibercept N=315
pivotal_trials.result: VABYSMO Q8W and Variable non-inferior to aflibercept Q8W. YOSEMITE mean BCVA change: VABYSMO Q8W 10.7 (97.5% CI 9.4, 12.0), Variable 11.6 (10.3, 12.9), aflibercept 10.9 (9.6, 12.2); RHINE 11.8 (10.6, 13.0), 10.8 (9.6, 11.9), 10.3 (9.1, 11.4).

key_safety: Most common adverse reaction (≥5%) was conjunctival hemorrhage (7%). Other common reactions (≥1%) included vitreous floaters (3%), retinal pigment epithelial tear (3% AMD), intraocular pressure increased (3%), eye pain (3%), and intraocular inflammation (2%). Potentially serious risks include endophthalmitis and retinal detachments, increase in intraocular pressure, and thromboembolic events.
target_moa: Humanized bispecific antibody that inhibits two pathways by binding VEGF-A and Ang-2; VEGF-A inhibition suppresses endothelial cell proliferation, neovascularization and vascular permeability, while Ang-2 inhibition is thought to promote vascular stability.
modality: Bispecific (humanized bispecific IgG1 antibody, CrossMAb format)

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is similar to that of other approved drugs for these indications.
